name: Product UGC review / testimonial
summary: Golden set for an authentic talking-head creator review: a problem-mirror hook, photoreal handheld realism, consistent product identity, and natural VO vs. the AI-slop face, drifting product, and ad-vibe failures.

examples.label: good
features: Hook in the first 0-3s mirrors the viewer's problem before naming the product (scroll-stop earned)
Photoreal handheld realism: skin pores, flyaways, slight asymmetry, natural single-source light — not a beauty-filtered AI face
Product identity is consistent across every shot (locked master ref passed on each generation)
VO register is natural and on-language for the target audience; lip-sync lands
Reads as a real creator capture, not a branded ad: no designed motion-graphics overlay on the b-roll
examples.notes: Photoreal-still register + super-original product lock + anti-ad-vibe. The ugc-ad skill carries the shooting-script shape.

examples.label: acceptable
features: Authentic delivery and a clear hook, but one mid-clip shows mild product drift (label/shape slightly off)
Realism mostly holds with one slightly glossy close-up
VO natural but pacing sags briefly in the middle third
examples.notes: Ships for testing; flag the product-drift shot for a re-roll against the locked ref.

examples.label: bad
features: Beauty-filtered AI face: enlarged eyes, reshaped jawline, plastic skin — the classic AI-slop tells
Product morphs between shots (different label / shape / color) because no master ref was locked
Hook opens on the product/logo instead of the viewer's problem, so it reads as an ad and gets scrolled
Robotic or accent-slipped VO (e.g. Kling --audio used for a non-English target, which drifts)
Designed brand motion-graphics slapped over handheld b-roll, killing the UGC authenticity
examples.notes: AI-slop image tells + identity drift + ad-vibe are the recurring failure cluster. Kling --audio is EN-only; confirm target language before defaulting.
